### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via aiExposed (symbol, a field of interface McpActionSummary))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via aiExposed (symbol, a field of interface McpActionSummary))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `211531ed93958127e098a7ba78f9c1f90b5971a2` — the merge of head `91f77a3413217b9efdc539dc093b794c06eda396` into base `ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 211531ed93958127e098a7ba78f9c1f90b5971a2 && git checkout 211531ed93958127e098a7ba78f9c1f90b5971a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 91f77a3413217b9efdc539dc093b794c06eda396 && git checkout -B drift-repro ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585 && git merge --no-ff 91f77a3413217b9efdc539dc093b794c06eda396

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ed0e71db94a73acc02512ff2ee0655106d02e585` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `55f4e1869506310aa84efcf05a513fd2654842ab`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution-destructive.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-system-object-exposure.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/27681-mcp-system-object-action-exposure.md + packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts (the `ai` block), packages/spec/src/kernel/stored-metadata-body-objects.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the REST door), packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-body-reads.test.ts (the #21594 pins), packages/mcp/src/index.ts, docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md (D4 and its amended note), docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx

Ruling under review: 6513869839, letter B, maintainer 「同意」 at 2026-10-30T02:59Z, parameter 2 amended by 6513938013 (declarations to #27900), parameter 3 carried by #27908 (claim amendment 6514100238). Inputs: card #27681 and every comment, the PR body, file list, comments and net diff against `main`, the head's check-runs, and the cited code on the head. Adversarial reading; the dispatch order and the seat's conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The predicate is per ACTION, keyed on the action's own flag and nothing else — holds.** `systemObjectActionExposureError` (`action-execution.ts`) answers `null` for a non-`sys_*` object; for a `sys_*` object it refuses unless `action.ai.exposed === true` (strict boolean). A description-only `ai` block, `exposed: 'true'`, `ActionAiSchema`'s default (`exposed: z.boolean().default(false)`), and any object-level or inherited value do not open it: the spec's `ObjectSchema` carries no `ai` block and no runtime path copies one onto an action (grep of object-level `ai` propagation on the head: none). The refusal sentence for the unflagged case keeps "is on a system object … and is not exposed via MCP", so the pre-existing pins still match it.
2. **Four sites, one predicate, no fifth path — holds.** `invokeBusinessAction` (first gate after resolution), the runtime bridge `listActions`, `resumeAdmissionRefusal`, and the tool layer (`isListableAction` for `list_actions` and the `run_action` pre-check that consults the bridge's listing) all read the same fact. A grep of `isSystemObjectName`, `isSystemObject(` and the `sys_` prefix regex over the head's non-test sources finds only these two files plus `packages/lint` (a static posture lint, not a door). The AI tool registry that materialises `action_*` tools is cloud-side, `packages/mcp` resources list no actions, and `domains/ai.ts` serves none. The object tools' `guard` (describe_object, query_records, …) keeps the name rule — objects, not actions, outside the ruling. The `run_action` pre-check matches on `name` and `objectName` exactly; a same-named action on another object does not admit (pinned).
3. **Behind every gate — holds; MCP is a superset of REST.** `invokeBusinessAction` on the head runs predicate → `isHeadlessInvokableAction` → `actionAiExposureError` → ADR-0066 D4 `actionPermissionError` → ADR-0126 §8 `disabledActionRefusal` → ADR-0104 D2 `enforceActionParams` → HITL `actionConfirmationRefusal` → `loadActionSubjectRecord` under the caller's RLS → `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` → the same-origin api forward as the caller. The diff changes only the first guard's predicate; the order is byte-for-byte the one on `main`. The REST door (`domains/actions.ts`) runs anonymous baseline → D4 → activation → params → subject load → forward, with the same shared helpers; the MCP bridge already requires a resolved principal (`userId` or `isSystem`). So no `sys_*` action is reachable over MCP that REST would refuse the same principal, and MCP adds the `ai.exposed` and confirmation gates REST does not have.
4. **Ruling parameter 1 (no deployment bypass) — holds.** `allowSystemObjects` is read only in `mcp-http-tools.ts`; the runtime predicate does not read it, so with it on the tool layer lists what the bridge serves and the runtime bridge still refuses every unflagged `sys_*` action. No env var or option was added.
5. **`resume_run` inference — accepted.** `McpActionBridge.resumeRun`'s contract text and the tool description already promised run_action's gates; the name-keyed copy would have let an agent start an exposed `sys_*` screen flow with `run_action` and be refused on the screen it was handed. The principal check (`trigger.userId` must equal the caller's `userId`, run `paused`) sits before the admission gates and is unchanged, so a flagged run cannot be resumed by another principal (pre-existing pin), and an unflagged action's run is refused 403 with the system-object sentence before the engine is asked (new pin).
6. **Stored-metadata family — refusal list exact and justified; the flag cannot open it.** `STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS` is the spec's one definition (`sys_metadata`, `sys_metadata_history`), consulted through `isStoredMetadataBodyObject`, no second list; the predicate refuses the family before it reads the flag, so `ai.exposed: true` on such an action is inert (pinned for every member). The #21594 pins in `stored-metadata-body-reads.test.ts` (flagged family actions: message names the action and "system object", no record load, no handler run) still hold against the new sentence. The ruling opened identity actions and named no family table, so keeping the family closed is the conservative reading and is written at the predicate.
7. **`McpActionSummary.aiExposed` — additive, nothing breaks.** Optional field on the published interface (exported via `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`); the only in-repo consumer is `isListableAction`. `summarizeAction` emits it only when `ai.exposed === true`, like `operation`; every action the runtime bridge lists already passes `actionAiExposureError`, so every listed summary carries it (asserted). A third-party bridge that omits it keeps every `sys_*` action hidden and refused, exactly as before.
8. **#27900 and #27908 — nothing slipped in, nothing silently claimed.** The diff touches no `packages/platform-objects` file and no audit code; the dogfood sets the test-only `ai` block on the in-process `SysUser` module before boot and restores it in `afterAll`, and asserts the platform declaration is still absent. The PR body states parameter 3 is not here and names #27908; the `[action-audit]` log line it mentions is pre-existing and untouched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` 18.2.0 → `patch`; `@objectstack/mcp` 18.2.0 → `patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no authorable key moves: `ai.exposed` pre-exists; `aiExposed` is a wire summary field, not metadata), and `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch` per Post-Task Checklist step 3. `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` — the arm reads as `widening` (`readArmToken` accepts the colon after the token), and the widening is real: the published `McpActionSummary` type and the MCP tools' accept-set grow. Changeset carries both declaration lines and the ruling reference; PR body matches. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Served-tier.** The brief asked for `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the PR's committed file list derives no path face (no `packages/spec/src` schema, no governed path) and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②` line, which reads `yes (widening)` ⇒ the declaration face, whose one standing token is `TIER_DEFAULT` (exact, never a floor, ruling 6159870311). The record carries the face's token; the ①–④ content is the full reading the brief ordered.
- **Dev deviation — Clause-②.** Claim 6514015162 declared `no`; the PR declares `yes (widening)`. The PR is right: a published type and a wire accept-set widen. The claim's `no` was the error; the dev flagged it in the report.
- **Dev deviation — branch name.** `claude/project-thread-qid1f1` (platform-assigned) rather than `claude/issue-27681-*`; declared in the acceptance notes; `Fixes #27681` carries the discoverability; the Duplicate Fix Guard may warn.
- **Dev deviation — ADR-0066 D4 closing note deferred.** The ruling allows a follow-up card with the pointer, and the PR body says so, but no card number is given in the PR body or the report, and D4's amended note still reads "stay off MCP … card #27681 carries it". Should-fix: file the follow-up and name its number on the PR before landing.
- **Docs drift (the dispatch seat's ACCEPT remit; flagged here because the hunks reverse what the pages state).** `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` ("System objects (`sys_*`) are held back fail-closed") and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` troubleshooting row ("it targets a `sys_*` object (held back fail-closed for every type, api included — #27681 tracks that gap)") now state the reversed rule, and `list_actions` output gained `aiExposed`. Should-fix: correct in this PR or a docs-only follow-up. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed by rule (kind `none`, no narrowing arm). The drift check named only `authorization.mdx` (via the `buildMcpBridge` symbol); that page's text is still accurate.
- **Parameter 3 → #27908, parameter 2 → #27900:** out of scope by the ruling's own text, and neither is claimed done here (see ① item 8).
- **Tests and ablation.** Nine legs reported; the committed tests pin each of the four sites in both directions (runtime: 3 predicate + 2 listing + 2 unflagged run + 4 flagged run through D4 / 409 / 428 / confirmed; resume ±; tool layer: 3 list + 5 run; dogfood: list, refused by name twice, 428, 409, member refused by the target, confirmed ban) and the moved pins are named. Not pinned: `resume_run` on a family table (covered by the predicate unit test) and `allowSystemObjects: true` end to end against the runtime bridge (structural: the runtime reads no option). Acceptable.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-30T05:00Z:** 53 runs, 38 `success`, 15 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 in progress; every required context present on the head is `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and its 8 shards, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI; the UI lint/type/build legs are path-skipped).
- `open_questions`: none declared; none raised by this reading. PR author is the relay identity; no login note owed. Local runs: none (template prints only).

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` — one exported predicate, its three runtime callers named in its doc, the family exemption citing the spec's one set, no `??` alias or shim (no ADR-0087 entry owed), and `summarizeAction` attesting only on the strict boolean. The doc comment's claim about gate order holds against the function body. The unused `_deps` matches the sibling gate signatures. Holds.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` — listing and resume adopt the predicate; the `isSystemObjectName` import is removed with no remaining use; `summarizeAction` is the one producer of the attestation. Holds.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` — `isListableAction` is the one predicate for list and run; the refusal sentence names both admission conditions; the header and the `allowSystemObjects` doc state the option's reach. The run pre-check re-lists on every `sys_*` run with an explicit `objectName` — one extra bridge call, acceptable for this class of call and cheaper than a new bridge method. Holds.
- The six test files — each site pinned admit and refuse, gates after admission pinned, moved pins named in the PR body; the dogfood mutates in-process only, restores declaration and env, and is an isolated file. Holds.
- `.changeset/27681-mcp-system-object-action-exposure.md` — both declarations, ruling reference, `patch` on both packages; the body states what still runs behind the flag and the day-one no-op. Holds.
- Cited code: `action.zod.ts` (`exposed` default false, `description` required when exposed) is what the predicate assumes; `stored-metadata-body-objects.ts` is the single family source; `domains/actions.ts` confirms REST's gates are a subset of MCP's; ADR-0011 (opt-in default off, permission and confirmation parity) and ADR-0066 D4 (one gate, two surfaces) are honoured, D4's amended note awaiting its dated closing note.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: (1) the two docs pages above; (2) file and name the ADR-0066 D4 follow-up card on the PR.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `91f77a3413217b9efdc539dc093b794c06eda396`
Local-runs: none
Scope: content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`systemObjectActionExposureError`, `actionAiExposureError`, `summarizeAction`, the `invokeBusinessAction` gate order), packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts (`listActions`, `resumeAdmissionRefusal`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`isListableAction`, the `list_actions` handler, the `run_action` pre-check, every `allowSystemObjects` read), content/docs/api/index.mdx, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, content/docs/releases/v15.mdx, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md

Delta review, carrying 6515376004 (PASS on `55f4e186`, rendered 2026-10-30T05:00Z) to this head. The delta is one commit, `91f77a34` "docs(ai): a sys_* action is exposed over MCP on its own ai.exposed, the family stays refused": 2 files, +18 −4, both under `content/docs/ai/`. Inputs: the diff `55f4e186..91f77a34`, the PR body as patched at 2026-10-30T05:13Z, claim amendment 6515405353 on #27681, follow-up card #27956, this head's check-runs, and the cited code read on this head. Every judgment of 6515376004 not restated below is adopted unchanged: the code tree at this head is byte-identical to the one it reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **No code moved — holds.** `git diff --stat` across the delta names exactly `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`; no package source, test, changeset or governed path is touched. 6515376004 ① 1–8 and ④ therefore stand as judgments of this head's code.
2. **`actions-as-tools.mdx` "What gets exposed" states the predicate as written — holds.** The paragraph's four claims are each read off `systemObjectActionExposureError` on this head: (a) a `sys_*` action is offered "only on its own `ai.exposed: true`" — the predicate answers `null` for a `sys_*` object only on `action?.ai?.exposed === true`, a strict boolean, nothing inherited; (b) "the object's name is not a second opt-in to clear" — the name decides only that the predicate is consulted, not its answer; (c) "no deployment switch opens one that is not flagged" — `allowSystemObjects` is read at two sites in `mcp-http-tools.ts` (the object-tool guard and the action-tool filter) and nowhere in the runtime, so with it on the tool layer stops filtering but the runtime bridge still refuses every unflagged `sys_*` action in `listActions`, `invokeBusinessAction` and `resumeAdmissionRefusal`; (d) "then runs behind every gate below, as on any other object" — the gate order in `invokeBusinessAction` is predicate → headless-invokable → `ai.exposed` → ADR-0066 D4 → ADR-0126 §8 activation → ADR-0104 D2 params → confirmation → subject load under the caller's RLS → denied-load refusal → forward, unchanged from `main`. The "one exception" sentence matches the predicate's first branch: `isStoredMetadataBodyObject` (the spec's one set, `sys_metadata` and `sys_metadata_history`) is refused before the flag is read, with the refusal text sending the caller to the metadata API — the page's wording.
3. **`list_actions` row: `aiExposed: true` on every item — holds for this runtime.** `summarizeAction` emits `aiExposed: true` only when `ai.exposed === true`; the runtime `listActions` pushes a summary only after `actionAiExposureError` (which requires the same strict `true`) and `actionPermissionError` both answer `null`; the tool handler returns `textResult({ actions: visible, totalCount })` with the summaries unmapped, with or without `allowSystemObjects`. So every item a client receives from the ObjectStack runtime carries the field, and the parenthesis "the author's opt-in, attested by the bridge" is the right attribution — the tool layer never sees a declaration. A third-party bridge behind the published `registerActionTools` may omit it (then every `sys_*` action stays hidden, as before); the page documents the runtime, and the published-interface contract is stated in the `mcp-http-tools.ts` header, not owed on this page.
4. **`connect-mcp.mdx` default-exposure bullet — holds; one nit.** The five gates it names behind the flag map one to one onto the code: `requiredPermissions` → `actionPermissionError` (D4); "the installation's action switch" → `disabledActionRefusal` (ADR-0126 §8, 409); "its param contract" → `enforceActionParams` (ADR-0104 D2); `ai.requiresConfirmation` → `actionConfirmationRefusal` (428); "the target's own authorization" → the same-origin `api` forward as the caller. The parenthesis does not name the subject load under the caller's RLS, which the sentence's "every gate behind the flag still runs" covers; a nit, not a fix. "No deployment switch opens an unflagged one", the family clause and the `aiExposed: true` attestation sentence are the same three facts as item 2–3. The bullet above it — objects: "except `sys_*` system objects, which are blocked fail-closed" — remains true of the object tools, whose guard keeps the name rule (6515376004 ① 2); the two bullets now state the two different rules for the two different tool families, which is the actual tree.
5. **`connect-mcp.mdx` troubleshooting row — holds.** The old clause ("it targets a `sys_*` object (held back fail-closed for every type, api included — #27681 tracks that gap)") is replaced by "it targets `sys_metadata` / `sys_metadata_history` (refused even when flagged — use the metadata API)". After the change the row's name-keyed reason is exactly the predicate's one name-keyed refusal; the other reasons in the row (`ai.exposed` not `true`, description shorter than 40 characters, non-headless type, `requiredPermissions`) are pre-existing and untouched.
6. **No other page or skill states the old rule — holds.** `git grep` on this head under `content/docs` and `skills`: `held back fail-closed` — zero hits; `#27681` — only the new sentence in `actions-as-tools.mdx`; `sys_*` and "system object" near MCP / `list_actions` / `run_action` / agent — `connect-mcp.mdx` line 242 (object tools, still true), `content/docs/api/index.mdx` line 17 ("Non-system objects exposed automatically …; actions additionally require the author's `ai.exposed` opt-in", true), `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` lines 198 and 203 (object introspection "system objects filtered out by default", true; `list_actions`/`run_action` "the same `ai.exposed` opt-in", true), `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` lines 69–72 (describes `isSystemObjectName` / `isSystemObject` as helpers keyed on the `sys_` name prefix — still true of both helpers on this head, which exist and key on the prefix; the page makes no claim about MCP admission), `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx` line 486 (a dated release note; history, not a rule). `allowSystemObjects` and `isSystemObjectName` appear in no docs or skill statement of the MCP rule. Nothing left to correct.
7. **Should-fix 1 of 6515376004 is closed by this delta** (items 2–5). **Should-fix 2 is closed:** #27956, filed 2026-10-30T05:02Z, open, `documentation`, unassigned and marked not a claim, quotes the D4 amended-note sentence, asks for a dated closing note in the ADR's own amendment style after #27940 merges, states the per-action rule and the family exception, and scopes out #27908 and #27900. The PR body names it ("carried by #27956, which runs after this PR merges") and names the docs commit by sha with its provenance (should-fix 1, amendment 6515405353). Amendment 6515405353 on #27681 adds the two pages to the claim's file surface and names #27956; the claim is otherwise unchanged.
8. **PR body on the delta — accurate, with one claim not re-run here.** "Docs only", "no code", and the two pages' summary match the diff. The body's "`pnpm docs:build` … exit 0 on `91f77a34`" is the dev's measurement; this record did not re-run it (`Local-runs: none`). On the head's check-runs, `Check Documentation Links` and `Flag docs affected by code changes` are `success`; `Build Docs` see ③.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6515376004: `@objectstack/runtime` `patch`, `@objectstack/mcp` `patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)`. The delta touches no package and leaves `.changeset/27681-mcp-system-object-action-exposure.md` byte-identical; a docs-only commit owes no changeset. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Served-tier.** `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the PR's 12-path committed file list at this head: no `packages/spec/src` schema, no governed register path (`content/docs/**` is not a register row), so the face is the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line ⇒ the declaration face ⇒ `TIER_DEFAULT`, as 6515376004 found. The declaration face carries no ④; the design reading of the code is 6515376004 ④, unchanged at this head.
- **Governance.** The delta adds no governed path; the PR is not a governed-surface PR before or after it. Still draft, head repo is the base repo.
